issues.detail: canoes (flap-track fairings): tone inverted in K-side views, too dark in A-side views
issues.problem: In every ANA photo of a canoe seen from above (7250, 7282, KN46, KN41), the upper part of the pod is the bright facet and the lower flank is darker. In w26K the order is reversed. The upper flank under the TE is mid grey (#8b8e8e at (620,280), #b0b4b6 at (640,310)), and a broad bright keel band at (600,340) #d4dade (L 217) is brighter than the wing skin (L 175). Each canoe therefore reads as a grey sock sitting on a white second fairing (ratA9/w26K_r9.png). The baked 0.45 belly term is overwhelmed by u_extBounce (0.69). Meanwhile, on the A side (w19A) the flanks fall to L 72-77, 0.45 of the skin against about 0.75 in KN41. The canoe has no consistent tone: a white keel in one view, charcoal teeth in another.
evidence: ref/web/exterior/b_alv_ANA77W_PY_IMG_7282-2-scaled.jpeg (canoes over the cloud deck: lit top, darker belly)
issues.fix: 11_exterior.js line 436: bake a monotonic top-to-belly ramp that does not fight the bounce: shadeVerts(B, vC, vN, (p, n) => n[1] > 0.3 ? 1 : n[1] > -0.4 ? 0.85 : lerp(0.85, 0.3, smooth(-0.4, -0.9, n[1]))). The flank sits near 0.85, which lifts w19A toward about 0.7 of the skin. The belly at 0.3 times the bounce lands below the flank. If the keel is still brighter than the flank, the lighting owner should scale u_extBounce by smoothstep(0.0, -0.6, N.y) * 0.6 for exterior materials with n.y < -0.5 (04_shaders.js:157), since the cloud deck cannot out-light the direct-sun flank.

issues.detail: wing surface: grime layer amplitude and character
issues.problem: The new streak texture is visible, but it is a uniform fine banding at the same strength everywhere (w17A, w19A, c_wing_panel), so it reads as brushed aluminium rather than wear. Residual SD is 2.3 % with a symmetric distribution (p5 -2.2 / p95 +3.3). The photos show 4.6-5.1 % with a dark skew (KN46 p5 -12 / p95 +7). The darkening there is localised: hinge lines, fastener heads (KN41 (490,830)), the flap TE and the exhaust-washed inboard flap (7250 (40-500, 620-900): 7.1 %). Across most of the fixed skin the photos are cleaner than the render's banding.
issues.fix: Lower the streak contrast of the global layer, LAYER_PARAMS for xSkin about x0.6 (shared 03_tex.js, one line). Move the darkening into localised per-vertex terms in the paintVerts loop: f *= 1 - 0.08 * smooth(0.35, 0, Math.abs(cx - hingeCx)) at the spoiler and flap hinge lines, and -10 % (not -6 %) on seg 2 for sp 8-11.8. In make_swatches x_skin, skew the tile dark: ground 1.0, sparse streak clusters at -8 to -14 % covering about 15 %, nothing above +3 %.

issues.detail: canoes: vertical streaks on the flanks
issues.problem: The canoes use `paint`, which now carries the triplanar grime layer. On the near-vertical flanks the triplanar projection samples the tile's other axis, so the streaks run vertically down the pod (visible as a curtain pattern in w26K and c_canoe_side). Real streaks on fairings run fore-aft with the flow.
issues.fix: 11_exterior.js line ~349: B.add(gLoft(secs, 3), ..., { ...paint, l: 0 }). Do the same for the pylon aft fairing loft at line ~430, which also uses `paint` on side-facing normals.

issues.problem: Unchanged. In c_nacelle_left the fan is a dark void with only the spinner tip showing. knav 7A _9 (480-540, 620-700) shows a bright silver spinner with the black spiral mark and a readable ring of wide-chord blades.
issues.fix: Raise the spinner albedo to about #b8bcc2 with metal 0.6, and set the fan blade disc to #3a3e44 instead of near-black, so the blade edges separate against the liner.

issues.problem: The swirl roundel and wordmark are now right in layout. They are drawn as raised tubes, though, which catch a highlight on one side and cast a dark edge on the other, so they read as embossed. The real mark is flat navy paint.
issues.fix: Halve the tube radius offset from the cowl, or flatten the tubes (scale the normal axis by 0.2), and set roughness 0.95 on the mark.

issues.problem: In s13A the underwing (left pane) is still saturated royal blue. In w19A the near skin (152) is still a little darker than the far skin (162); the photos run brighter near.
